text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

A study by Sydney University's Research Institute for Asia and the Pacific has found that less than one third of Australia's top companies are focused on creating business in East Asia despite a push by recent governments for improved business relationshis with the rapidly growing region. The survey interviewed the directors on the boards of 135 of Australia's top 200 listed companies. Page 1.

The AMP society will do battle with Abbey National Plc bank, Britain's second-largest mortgage lender, and Prudential Corp Plc, Britain's largest life insurer, for Scottish Amicable, which is expected to attract a winning bid of up to A$5 billion. AMP group development director Jonathan Schwartz said from London, AMP believes Scottish Amicable is one of a number of current opportunities that fulfils the company's criteria. Page 19.

The senior management team of brewer Lion Nathan has faced a reshuffle, with Australian division head Gordon Cairns to head both the Australian and New Zealand brewing operations. The company has also adopted a new marketing strategy in its latest bid to increase its sliding share of the Australian brewing market. Page 19.

Optus Communications chief executive officer Ziggy Switkowski is expected this week to tell the market the good news about the telecommunications carrier's strong December-half profit of A$59 million, yet this profit was wiped out by its A$78 million share of operating losses from its 46.5 per cent-owned Optus Vision cable TV business. The situation could see Optus quit the pay-TV business. Page 20.

RTZ-CRA is still waiting for formal notification from the Papua New Guinea Government about a proposed buyout of its 53.6 per cent stake in Bougainville Copper Ltd. On the weekend the PNG Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan offered to acquire the mine as a wa of ending the island's civil war. Australian-listed CRA Ltd is the major shareholder in Bougainville Copper and former operator of the now abandoned mine on the war-torn island. Page 4.

The Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry's national survey of business expectations of the March 1997 quarter reveals an improvement in business conditions over the past three months. However, it shows that small companies still lag behind larger ones in confidence and business activity and growth are still stagnant. The release of the survey comes days before the publication of the December-quarter national accounts which economists expect will show only slight growth in the economy. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Local Australian markets have followed the fall on Wall Street that saw the Dow Jones industrial average fall 47.33 points to 6877.74. As the All Ordinaries index lost 50.9 points in its past three trading sessions, it is expected to suffer another drop today following the fall out from US Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's questioning of the sustainability of the two-year-long surge in US stock prices. Page 17.

Federal Government intervention looks to be inevitable in a dispute over the commercialisation of the Australian Wheat Board that has divided the wheat industry. The industry is supposed to present Primary Industries Minister John Anderson with an agreed blueprint for the post-1999 structure of the AWB as part of a five-year industry plan this week. Failure to do this would mean the dispute would be solved by a Government-imposed solution. Page 17.

Under a complex strategy to raise funds in the United States, integrated telecommunications company Newsnet ITN Ltd is to delist from the Australian Stock Exchange. Under a deal with a private, US-based investment firm, Asia Pacific Holdings Corp, Newsnet will become a subsidiary of a new company, Newsnet ITN Holdings Ltd, which will then raise between A$7.5 and A$11 million through a US public offering. Page 19.

In a bid to cut costs and reposition its products, paper wholesaler Amcor Ltd has announced in the industry newsletter Ausnewz Pulp and Paper a restructure of its troubled merchant trading arms. The move will merge the back office operations of two of he company's three merchants, The Paper House and Tomasetti Paper. The third company, Dalton Fine Paper, will continue separate. Page 19.

The mining and rural sectors have angrily accused the Howard Government of breaking its promise on the diesel fuel rebate and trying to make extra savings from the scheme. In a Bill currently awaiting Senate debate, the Howard Government has proposed resrictions on eligibility to the diesel fuel rebate, a move which the Minerals Council says is a betrayal of the agreement reached in post-Budget consultations last year. Page 19.

Qantas and Aussie Airlines will this week request an extension to their negotiations over access to domestic airport terminals. Aussie Airlines wants access to terminal space at five domestic airports leased to Qantas by the Federal Airports Corp. After a series of court battles, a deadline had been set by February 28 by the Federal Airports Corp for sub-leases to be signed, but it is expected to grant the extension of talks requested by both companies. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The AMP Society has confirmed its intentions to move into the European market before its planned demutulisation by joining the A$4.1 billion bidding war for United Kingdom life insurer Scottish Amicable Life Assurance Society. AMP lodged a formal bid on riday and its firepower to make such a large bid sits in its current UK-based businesses of Pearl Assurance and London Life in the form of A$2.3 billion in cash. Page 37.

Stockbroking firms pitching for the top management roles in the Telstra float have given the Federal Government valuation figures for the national carrier of between A$30 and A$40 billion, figures that boost the government's chances of receiving more than $8 billion from the partial privatisation of Telstra. Page 37.

Downing Centre Local Court Magistrate Malcolm Beveridge found on Friday that former Aust Wide Property Trust group managing director Henry Townsing had no case to answer on charges that he used his position to redeem A$98,075 worth of units prior to trust assets being frozen in July 1990. Page 39.

The New South Wales Government has asked for expressions of interest from legal firms to assist in the process of privatising the NSW TAB. While the Government is yet to reveal its view on a possible structure of a TAB privatisation, a letter circulated ast week from the government's asset sales task force invited law firms to submit proposals on the best possible privatisation structure. Page 39.

In a closed session on Friday, lawyers for the Seven Network asked Justice Hunter of the Supreme Court to allow the Network to amend its action to argue that the other shareholders in Optus Vision had shown bad faith and were guilty of fraud in the used of ther powers as joint-venture partners. Page 39.

Economists have warned that share prices are expected to come under pressure today following falls in the United States over the weekend. Meanwhile the Reserve Bank of Australia may have to review interest rates when a stack of United States and local data is due to be released this week. However, an easing of rates in Australia after Tuesday's meeting of the Reserve Bank board seems unlikely. Page 39.
THE AGE

AMP Society confirmed on the weekend it has filed a bid for British life insurer Scottish Amicable Life Assurance Society, and will be up against two other financial services giants, UK companies Abbey National Bank and Prudential Corporation. AMP said i was prepared to spend around A$4.3 billion to expand into Europe. Page B1.

Papua New Guinea Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan confirmed his government will attempt to purchase the abandoned Panguna copper mine on Bougainville from mining giant RTZ-CRA. T he mine, which RTZ-CRA owns about 53.6 per cent of, was closed down in the midle of 1989 following a series of armed attacks that forced the company to withdraw its staff. Page B1.

Jurg Bollag, the man whose involvement in businessman Alan Bond's international financial dealings is under suspicion and has been ordered to be examined under oath for a week in April at the office of the Public Prosecutor in Bollag's home, the Swiss tow of Zug. The examination of Bollag comes three years after the Federal Attorney General Department made a formal request to Swiss authorities to interview Bollag and obtain documents relating to his dealings with Bond. Page B1.

Australia remains the only major market in the world where Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation is not investing in satellite television. However, following 1 July this year, when Australia's telecommunications market becomes deregulated, there will be strong temptation for the company to make a satellite-based play for the pay TV market. Page B3.

Lynas Gold NL has over the last ten years explored the WA Pilbara region for gold deposits. For the last three years it has been producing gold from the Lynas Find project. Discovered in 1987 the project took seven years to bring to production on account of a cash squeeze and the company's insistence on its independence from a dominant partner. Lynas Gold Nl is now poised to take control of production in the region. Page B3.

Hopes held by radio and television conglomerate Southern Cross Broadcasting to better its low earnings from last year have been dashed by soft advertising conditions. Flat advertising revenue from the first-half to 31 December show a net profit fall of 2 per cent to $4.5 million. The second half of the financial year is expected to show some signs of recovery. Page B3.
